title: Meeus, J. (1998). Astronomical Algorithms, 2nd edition, Willmann-Bell, chapter 44 Positions of the Satellites of Jupiter
note: The printed chapter was not read. Its two methods are quoted from two implementations that state they follow it: soniakeys/meeus jupitermoons.go and PyMeeus JupiterMoons.py. Cited for the algorithm, with the transcription caveat.

title: Keys, S. (2013). meeus/v3/jupitermoons/jupitermoons.go, Go implementation of Astronomical Algorithms chapter 44 (MIT licence)
note: Read in full. Third-party reimplementation. Source of the quoted low-accuracy method (Positions) and of the E5 method with differential light-time constants 17295, 21819, 27558, 36548 and perspective divisor 2095. The package documents its validation by tests that reproduce Meeus's worked examples.

title: Lutz, M., Scholz, S., Serra, V. and Veigl, S. (2020). PyMeeus, pymeeus/JupiterMoons.py (LGPL-3.0)
note: Read in full. Third-party reimplementation of the chapter 44 high-accuracy method. Source of the solar (R = 0) variant for eclipses and of the Y scale factor 1.071374 used in its eclipse and occultation tests.

title: Lieske, J. H. (1977). Theory of motion of Jupiter's Galilean satellites. Astronomy and Astrophysics 56, 333-352
note: First page read from the ADS scan: summary and introduction. Source of the 49 arbitrary constants, the description as a revitalisation of Sampson (1921), and Sampson's accuracy goal of 2, 3.3, 5.2 and 9.1 km.

title: Lieske, J. H. (1986). A collection of Galilean satellite eclipse observations, 1652-1983: Part I. Astronomy and Astrophysics 154, 61-76
note: First two pages read from the ADS scan. History of the Delisle, Pingre and Delambre collections and of Sampson's 1910 search for them.

title: Lieske, J. H. (1998). Galilean satellite ephemerides E5. Astronomy and Astrophysics Supplement Series 129, 205-217
note: Abstract only, as given in a search-result description of the publisher page. The full text was not read because the publisher refused automated access. Cited for E5 being produced for the Galileo mission, in B1950 with J2000 results available, and recommended over E3 and E4.

title: Arlot, J.-E. (1982). New constants for Sampson-Lieske theory of the Galilean satellites of Jupiter. Astronomy and Astrophysics 107, 305-310
note: First page read from the ADS scan. Source of the G-5 constants from 8856 photographic observations 1891 to 1978 and of the E-1 and E-2 provenance.

title: Thuillot, W. (1983). Theorie des phenomenes des satellites galileens de Jupiter: une representation par les polynomes de Tchebychev. Astronomy and Astrophysics 127, 63-67
note: Pages 1 to 3 read from the ADS scan (in French). Source of the cone equations with an ellipsoidal Jupiter, the phase correction of 3 min (Io) and 6 min (Callisto), the light-time rules, the Chebyshev form and its 51 s maximum error.

title: IMCCE, /pub/ephem/satel/phenjupiter/README (2021 September)
note: Read in full. Event codes, TT time scale, mid-event convention, the theory used for each range of years (G-5 to 2014, L1 2015 to 2022, Lainey 2021 after), and the TT-UT table.

title: IMCCE, phenE.2026, ftp_jupiter_Events_UT_2026.txt and xyE.2026 (2025-03-31)
note: Read the headers and first months. Eclipse times to 0.1 min, other events to 1 min in the TT file. UT version rounded to the minute with TT-UT = 69 s. Monthly X, Y of eclipse positions.

title: IMCCE, /pub/ephem/satel/phenjupCDT/README (1999-02-22)
note: Read in full. Chebyshev polynomials for the phenomena as published in the Connaissance des Temps.

title: Lainey, V., IMCCE /pub/ephem/satel/galilean/L1/L1.1/ README (2007-05-07)
note: Read in full. Fit to observations 1891 to 2003, accuracy of a few hundred km for 1970 to 2010, TDB from epoch JD 2433282.5, output frames and units.

title: Lainey, V., IMCCE /pub/ephem/satel/NOE/JUPITER/2021/ README and NOE-5-2021.tpc (2021-02-04)
note: Read in full. Data fitted (Earth-based from 1891 including radar, HST, Voyager, Galileo), coverage 1880 to 2049, the long variant NOE-5-2021L for 1650 to 2000, GM values and pole.

title: Lainey, V., Duriez, L. and Vienne, A. (2004). New accurate ephemerides for the Galilean satellites of Jupiter. I. Numerical integration of elaborated equations of motion. Astronomy and Astrophysics 420, 1171-1183
note: Abstract read (HAL hal-03786468). Full text not read.

title: Lainey, V., Arlot, J.-E. and Vienne, A. (2004). New accurate ephemerides for the Galilean satellites of Jupiter. II. Fitting the observations. Astronomy and Astrophysics 427, 371-376
note: Abstract read (HAL hal-03786055). Names the fitted ephemerides L1 and the observation span from 1891. Full text not read.

title: Lainey, V., Duriez, L. and Vienne, A. (2006). Synthetic representation of the Galilean satellites' orbital motions from L1 ephemerides. Astronomy and Astrophysics 456, 783-788
note: Abstract read (HAL record). The IMCCE phenjupiter README cites the same paper as 2007. Source of the quasi-periodic Fourier series that Stellarium ports as L1.2.

title: Lainey, V., Arlot, J.-E., Karatekin, O. and Van Hoolst, T. (2009). Strong tidal dissipation in Io and Jupiter from astrometric observations. Nature 459, 957-959
note: Read in the reprint bound into Lainey's habilitation (IMCCE). Observations 1891 to 2007, post-fit residuals 0.02 to 0.15 arcsec, mutual events about 0.025 arcsec, Sampson-Lieske internal errors of a few hundred km, 1 arcsec about 3000 km at Jupiter.

title: Lainey, V. Habilitation a diriger des recherches, IMCCE (PDF of collected papers)
note: Read the NOE description and the Nature 2009 reprint. Undated in the extracted text.

title: Stellarium, src/core/planetsephems/l12.h and l12.c, and EphemWrapper.cpp (master at commit 77d52ea)
note: Read. L1.2 theory of Lainey, Vienne and Duriez ported from FORTRAN, TT JD input, Jupiter-centred VSOP87 frame in au, time argument JD - 2433282.5; the four Galilean moons always use it.

title: NAIF, generic_kernels/spk/satellites/jup365.cmt (BVS/NAIF, 2021-03-14)
note: Read the header. JUP365.26 global fit, DE440 planets, 1600 to 2200, RADIUS 71492 km, Chebyshev interpolation error 16 m, GM values. The .bsp is 1,136,581,632 bytes.

title: NAIF, generic_kernels/spk/satellites/a_old_versions/jup310.cmt (R. A. Jacobson, released 2013-11-25)
note: Read in full. JUP310.2 fit to Earth-based and spacecraft data through 2013, DE430, 1799 to 2200, RADIUS 71492 km, Chebyshev error 0.5 m.

title: Saquet, E., Emelyanov, N., Robert, V., Arlot, J.-E. et al. (2018). The PHEMU15 catalogue and astrometric results of the Jupiter's Galilean satellite mutual occultation and eclipse observations made in 2014-2015. MNRAS 474, 4730-4739
note: Read in full from the UNESP repository copy. Campaign statistics 1985 to 2015, the photometric model, the Emelyanov reduction equations, NOE-5-2010-GAL and JUP310 residuals.

title: Arlot, J.-E., Emelyanov, N. et al. (2014). The PHEMU09 catalogue and astrometric results of the observations of the mutual occultations and eclipses of the Galilean satellites of Jupiter made in 2009. Astronomy and Astrophysics 572, A120
note: Abstract read through the HAL API (hal-01098147). Full text not read: the publisher and HAL pages refused automated access.

title: Emelyanov, N., Arlot, J.-E. et al. (2022). The PHEMU21 catalogue and astrometric results of the observations of the mutual occultations and eclipses of the Galilean satellites of Jupiter made in 2021. MNRAS 516, 3685-3691
note: Abstract read through the HAL API (insu-03850262). 84 light curves, rms O-C 49 and 48 mas. Full text not read.

title: Arlot, J.-E. et al. (2006). The PHEMU97 catalogue of observations of the mutual phenomena of the Galilean satellites of Jupiter. Astronomy and Astrophysics 451, 733-737
note: Abstract read through the HAL API. 275 observations of 148 events from 42 sites.

title: Arlot, J.-E. et al. (2009). The PHEMU03 catalogue of observations of the mutual phenomena of the Galilean satellites of Jupiter. Astronomy and Astrophysics
note: Abstract read from the VizieR catalogue record (Arlot+, 2009). 377 observations of 118 events from 42 sites. Volume and pages not confirmed.

title: Emelyanov, N. V. and Arlot, J.-E. (2008). The natural satellites ephemerides facility MULTI-SAT. Astronomy and Astrophysics 487, 759-765
note: Abstract read through the HAL API. Pages from the citation in Tsumura et al. Full text not read.

title: Catani, L. M., Assafin, M., Morgado, B. E. et al. (2023). The 2021 mutual phenomena involving the Galilean satellites of Jupiter and the inner satellite Thebe. MNRAS, doi:10.1093/mnras/stad3006 (arXiv:2310.00807)
note: Read in the arXiv version. Read sections 1 and 4 to 8. DE440 plus JUP365, Oren-Nayar reflectance, solar limb darkening of Hestroffer and Magnan, chi-square fit of about 900 simulated curves per event, 5 mas (15 km) average uncertainty.

title: So, C. W. et al. (2022). The photometric observation of the quasi-simultaneous mutual eclipse and occultation between Europa and Ganymede on 22 August 2021. Icarus 392, 115348 (2023) (arXiv:2212.05215)
note: Read in the arXiv version. Read sections 1 to 3. MULTI-SAT predicted 242 PHEMU21 events, 192 observable 3 March to 16 November 2021, from Lainey et al. (2009) theory; effective penumbra radius 17 per cent above the umbra.

title: Vasundhara, R., Selvakumar, G. and Anbazhagan, P. (2017). Analysis of mutual events of Galilean satellites observed from VBO during 2014-15. MNRAS, doi:10.1093/mnras/stx437 (arXiv:1704.03518)
note: Read in the arXiv version. Read sections 1 to 3. Hapke parameters, USGS albedo maps, photocentre shifts, the impact-parameter reduction equations, and residuals against L2 (NOE-5-2010-GAL-a2.bsp).

title: Morgado, B. et al. (2019). APPROX - mutual approximations between the Galilean moons. The 2016-2018 observational campaign. MNRAS 482, 5190 (arXiv:1811.02913)
note: Abstract read in the arXiv version. 104 central instants from 66 mutual approximations, 11.3 mas internal precision, against about 100 mas for classical CCD astrometry.

title: Thuillot, W. and Tanga, P. (1997). Bibliography on various works related to the mutual events of the Galilean satellites. PHEMU Technical Note 8, IMCCE
note: Read sections 1 and 2. History of predictions and analyses for 1973 and 1979, including the 91 light curves of Aksnes and Franklin (1976).

title: Arlot, J.-E. (2014). The campaigns of observation of the mutual phenomena of the Galilean satellites: the campaign 2014-2015 (slides, IMCCE)
note: Read the opening slides. Equinox recurrence for Jupiter, Saturn and Uranus.

title: Oksanen, A. (2026-02-07). PHEMU havaitseminen (slides, Ursa Aurinkokuntatapaaminen, in Finnish)
note: Read in full. Practitioner presentation. Lists 305 predicted events from 11 May 2026 to 10 August 2027 from the SAI natural satellites service, and quotes Saquet et al. (2018).

title: IMCCE Natural Satellites Data Center, Guide for the phenomena of the natural planetary satellites
note: Read in full. Definitions, half-flux timing convention, the 10 km per second of time rule, time-scale advice.

title: IMCCE Natural Satellites Data Center, README_EC_NSDB for Galilean eclipse observations 1652 to 1983
note: Read in full. 16,802 eclipse observations from 426 sites, O-C and TQ conventions.

title: IMCCE, /pub/ephem/satel/phemu97/README (1996-05-15)
note: Read in full. Predictions of 469 mutual events for 1997 with local visibility files.

title: Westfall, J. E. (2006). Timing the eclipses of Jupiter's Galilean satellites. ALPO observing instructions
note: Read pages 1 and 2. Table of penumbral widths, ingress and egress durations and eclipse durations; the 1 to 2 minute offset of visual timings from mid-event predictions; comparison standard E-2.

title: Nagoya City Science Museum, Jupiter Tool (Juptool) manual
note: Read. The program's own statement of method (Meeus chapter 44 high-accuracy method with truncations), centre-contact convention and 3 to 4 minute error.

title: Sky & Telescope (2008). Erratum: Jupiter's moons for May 2008
note: Not read: the page refused automated access. Reported secondhand that the magazine's tables are computed by the Bureau des Longitudes. Unconfirmed.

title: Bobis, L. and Lequeux, J. (2008). Cassini, Romer and the velocity of light. Journal of Astronomical History and Heritage 11, 97-105
note: Read pages 97 to 99. Longitude use of Jovian eclipses, Cassini's 1668 ephemerides, the 15 s and half-minute timing accuracies, the 22 August 1676 announcement and the 7 December 1676 publication.

title: Shorthill, R. W., Greene, T. F. and Smith, D. W. (1974). Atmospheric properties of Jupiter determined from Galilean satellite eclipse light curves. IAU Symposium proceedings, Cambridge University Press
note: Read in full. Twelve eclipse light curves in 30 colours with the Hale telescope, refractive tails, cloud-top cut-off near 9 magnitudes of darkening.

title: Tsumura, K. et al. (2014). Near-infrared brightness of the Galilean satellites eclipsed in Jovian shadow. ApJ 789, 122 (arXiv:1405.5280)
note: Read in the arXiv version. Abstract and introduction read. Eclipsed satellites at 1e-6 to 1e-7 of their normal brightness near 1.5 micrometres.
